headline: Cairn tests community reputation as shared memory for agent tools and services
summary: A September 2026 preprint presents Cairn, a community reputation service where agents check a tool, data source or peer before use and add a rubric-based rating afterward. Its time-decayed Beta scorer shrinks uncertain ratings toward neutral. In simulations averaged over 100 seeds, reported scores tracked responder accuracy with mean absolute deviation 0.017, but pooled ratings failed sharply when dishonest raters approached or exceeded a majority. A live-corpus retrieval test reached R@5 0.65 overall and only 0.34 for mostly negative entities, so failure reports were harder to retrieve. A judge-rated sample of 5,000 active Moltbook agents produced scores uncorrelated with platform karma. These are paper-reported system and judge results; the paper does not establish improved downstream task outcomes, and Sybil attacks remain an open threat.
